chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He forbade the walnut that the children bring from gambling, saying it should not be eaten, and said, 'It is sustenance (suh't).'

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Suh't (sustenance from gambling or uncertain sources)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating walnuts obtained from children's gambling in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits consuming walnuts brought by children from gambling, classifying them as *suh't*—sustenance derived from games of chance. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the purity of income, extending the concept of *suh't* beyond mere illicit gain to include items acquired through the mechanism of gambling, thereby linking material consumption to spiritual cleanliness.
